title: Find a command by a keyword in the manuals
summary: Linux and macOS keep a one-line description of every manual page. Search those descriptions for a word like 'copy' to find the command that does your task, then open its manual with man.

aliases.text: search man pages for a word
как найти нужную команду в терминале

prerequisites: A terminal window (Terminal on macOS, or a terminal app on Linux)
On Linux the man-db package and manual pages must be installed; minimal installs may lack them

steps.explain: Check that the search index works. You should see a one-line description of ls. If you see 'nothing appropriate' or 'command not found', the manual pages are missing: install the man-db package and its manual pages with your package manager.
steps.expect: On Linux: 'ls (1)               - list directory contents'. Any one-line description of ls is fine.

steps.explain: Search the one-line descriptions of all manual pages for a word that describes your task, such as 'copy'. Each result shows the command name, its manual section in brackets, and a short description. Pick the line that matches your goal. The output is cut to 20 lines.

placeholders.name: KEYWORD
placeholders.description: English word that describes the task

steps.expect: Lines such as 'cp (1)  - copy files and directories'. The name before the bracket is the command. 'copy: nothing appropriate.' means no match: try another word.

alternatives.explain: Same search with apropos, which prints the same lines. Add -s 1 to show only commands you type in Terminal (manual section 1).

placeholders.name: KEYWORD
placeholders.description: English word that describes the task

steps.explain: Open the full manual of the command you picked. Scroll with the arrow keys or the Space bar, and press q to quit.

placeholders.name: COMMAND
placeholders.description: Command name from the search results

steps.expect: The page starts with NAME, SYNOPSIS and DESCRIPTION sections. Press q to return to the prompt.

verify.expect: A file path such as /usr/share/man/man1/cp.1.gz (Linux) or a path ending in cp.1 (macOS). It shows that the manual exists.
